results.why: K38 scores whether a concrete, usable artifact (data/model suite/tool) is actually released versus vaguely promised or absent, which is the operative axis of T01 at abstract level, though K38 frames it as contribution value rather than reproduction support.

No candidate scores interpretive discussion as a whole (findings read against objectives/theory, alternative explanations, restrained conclusions, implications); candidates cover only disjoint fragments such as limitations (K49) or claim calibration (K56).
Nothing in the candidate set scores intervention/comparator description (components, dose, delivery, provider, arm similarity) or any analogue of it.

K46/K56 reward naming metrics and effect sizes and K17 rewards uncertainty, but none scores the definition, prioritization, and timing of outcome measures together with precision reporting, so each is only a fragment.

K17 and K50 both score exactly whether conclusions rest on one unreplicated run versus measured variation across seeds/checkpoints/runs with reported stability or uncertainty, which is T05's property in ML vocabulary.
K38 is the nearest but scores whether a reusable asset is offered, not the richness of its documentation, intended-use limits, known gaps, versioning, or long-term stewardship.

K38's axis — a concretely available, reusable artifact with scope for others to build on, versus vague or absent release — is substantially the same property as T07's availability-and-reusability judgment, minus T07's selection-rationale clause.
No candidate scores venue fit, scope match to the publication outlet, or baseline submission eligibility.

K04 scores whether the contribution is stated as an explicit difference from a named nearest prior method rather than against an undifferentiated field, which is T09's contrast-with-prior-work property, though K04 does not separately judge substantive originality.

No candidate scores whether the procedure and analysis are described completely enough (materials, preprocessing, controls, exclusion rules) for independent replication; K46/K56 score claim anchoring, a different property.
Ethics approvals, consent, PII, compensation, and conflicts of interest have no counterpart; K22 concerns using human judgments as evaluation data, not the ethics of collecting them.
No candidate scores length or format appropriateness; K05 explicitly normalizes out length, and K18/K53 score narrative coherence rather than concision.

K20 scores the ratio of claimed scope to demonstrated scope, penalizing universal claims evidenced narrowly and rewarding modest claims modestly evidenced — the same property as T13's accurate characterization of where findings apply and avoidance of over-general claims.
No candidate addresses prediction-model reporting standards such as study type, data sources, validation design, calibration, or discrimination.

K17 covers only the uncertainty/variation fragment; no candidate scores appropriateness and transparent reporting of statistical methods (assumption checks, tests, multiplicity control, software, model justification).

K04 scores situating the work against a named nearest prior method and K58 scores quantified comparison against a named strong baseline, together covering T16's differentiate-from-prior-art-and-compare-to-baselines property.
